title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 190 (Contract of employment with managing or whole-time directors)

content.overview: Section 190 requires every company to keep at its registered office a copy of every contract of service entered into by it with a managing or whole-time director, and where no such contract is in writing, a written memorandum setting out the terms of the contract. Members are entitled to inspect the copy or memorandum. The section is a transparency and inspection duty; appointment is governed by section 196 and remuneration limits by section 197.
content.glance: Copy of MD/WTD service contract (or written memorandum of terms if unwritten) kept at registered office; open to member inspection; distinct from appointment (s. 196) and remuneration (s. 197).
content.study: Every company shall keep at its registered office a copy of every contract of service entered into by it with a managing or whole-time director, and in case of a contract not being in writing, a written memorandum setting out the terms of the contract. The copies of the contract or the memorandum shall be open to inspection by any member of the company without payment of fee. Current-law framing: confirm MD or WTD status; ensure written contract or memorandum exists at the registered office; allow member inspection. Do not confuse with the appointment process under s. 196 or the remuneration ceiling under s. 197.

sections.heading: Document at Registered Office
sections.body: Copy of every contract of service with a managing or whole-time director, or a written memorandum of terms if the contract is not in writing, kept at the registered office.

sections.heading: Member Inspection
sections.body: Members may inspect the copy or memorandum without payment of fee.

sections.heading: Relationship to Appointment and Remuneration
sections.body: Section 190 is the inspection duty. Appointment is under s. 196; remuneration limits are under s. 197.

provisions.title: Contract of employment with managing or whole-time directors

examples.title: Unwritten terms
examples.body: A company engages a whole-time director on oral terms only and keeps no written memorandum at the registered office. Section 190 requires a written memorandum setting out the terms.

examples.title: Member inspection
examples.body: A member requests inspection of the MD’s service contract at the registered office. Section 190 entitles the member to inspect without fee.

hypotheticals.question: Does keeping the s. 190 document validate an appointment that breached s. 196?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 190 is a record-and-inspection duty. Validity of appointment is governed by section 196 (and related provisions), not by the mere presence of a service contract copy.

distinctions.title: Service-contract inspection (s. 190) vs appointment of MD/WTD (s. 196)
distinctions.left: Keep and allow inspection of the contract or memorandum
distinctions.right: How and for what term a managing or whole-time director is appointed

misconceptions.trap: Only written service contracts need to be kept; oral arrangements need nothing.
misconceptions.correction: If there is no written contract, a written memorandum setting out the terms must still be kept at the registered office.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 190 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm MD/WTD. II. Check contract or memorandum at registered office. III. Test member inspection. IV. Distinguish appointment/remuneration sections. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Status facts; document location; inspection; precise relief.

Not the appointment or remuneration section.
